title: Resolver session replay causing tenant mapping glitch during dedicated node recycle
creator: Lina Patel
description:
Summary:
A paying Dedicated customer reported intermittent cross-tenant DNS resolution where hostname A (tenant X) briefly resolved to an IP owned by tenant Y immediately after scheduled dedicated-node recycle. Impact is intermittent but reproducible under load; customers observed transient misbinding of hostname -> tenant mapping for 2-10s windows which caused request routing to surface other customers' endpoints in logs and triggered escalations.

Observed behavior and how to reproduce:
1) Start a heavy batch of short-lived connections from Tenant X to external resolvers (UDP 53) while the cluster autoscaler evicts a dedicated node.
2) Eviction triggers worker process respawn and NAT reassignment on the host; concurrently, a resolver socket in the runtime agent gets torn down and re-created.
3) Under these timing conditions we observed a replayed UDP DNS response being associated with the wrong conntrack tuple and attributed to Tenant Y's ephemeral SNAT port, causing the platform to record the name resolution under the wrong tenant and temporarily route followup flows incorrectly.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- The runtime egress stack reuses resolver sockets and ephemeral port ranges aggressively to save resources. During node recycle/worker handoff there is a small window where a DNS response can be processed after conntrack state has been rebound to a different tenant's SNAT range.
- The resolver response path lacked explicit tenant-context tagging for UDP transactions; the flow matching relied solely on conntrack tuples (srcIP:srcPort -> dst), which were transiently reused.
- A combination of accelerated port reuse (snat allocator heuristics under memory/port pressure) and an out-of-order processing path in the network agent allowed a replayed packet to be accepted and attributed incorrectly.

Impact and scope:
- Affects Dedicated customers using shared egress pools (default config), primarily during node evictions, autoscaler-driven resizes, or planned host maintenance.
- Customer-visible symptoms: transient misresolution, incorrect request logs showing other tenant hostnames/IPs, and failed application-level host validation in edge cases.
- Severity: P0 due to customer escalations and potential data-visibility concerns. No confirmed data exfiltration but violates tenant isolation guarantees while the window is open.

Proposed mitigations and fixes:
Immediate (hotfix / mitigations):
- Disable aggressive ephemeral port reuse for dedicated clusters via feature-flag (runtime.config: snat.ephemeral_reuse=false). Rollout as a near-term stopgap for high-risk customers. (Can be toggled per-tenant.)
- Add a conservative grace-window during node recycle where resolver responses are validated against a temporary responder nonce (generated per socket) to discard late-arriving replies.

Engineering fix (medium-term):
1) Tag UDP resolver transactions with tenant context at creation time and propagate that tag through the network agent to the conntrack matching layer. This ensures a late or replayed DNS response cannot be associated with a conntrack tuple that lacks the tenant tag.
2) Harden SNAT allocator to avoid immediate port reuse for at least N seconds after release when density > threshold. Configurable heuristic: min_ephemeral_hold_ms.
3) Add unit + integration tests that simulate node recycle and replayed UDP responses across namespaces.
4) Canary rollout plan: small percentage of dedicated clusters, monitor resolver error rate, tenant isolation metrics, and customer tickets.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- No transient cross-tenant name resolutions during controlled node evictions in canary clusters (end-to-end test).
- New telemetry surfaces resolver-replay-drop counts and tenant-tag-mismatch events.
- Hotfix flag available and applied to affected customers with documented mitigation playbook.
- Post-rollout audit confirms no customer sees mapping glitches for 72 hours in canary before wide rollout.

Artifacts / Links:
- Investigation notes (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/RESOLVER-SESSION-REPLAY
- Repro harness (internal gist with k8s job): https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-resolver-replay-2026
- Runtime PR implementing tenant tagging: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892 (draft)
- Customer escalation thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0GREED/escalations/2026-03-02
- Postmortem template (if needed): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1resolverpostmortem
